meetings.executive_summary: On March 3, 2023, the Durham City Council held the second day of its FY 2023-24 Budget Retreat at the Department of Water Management facility. City Manager Wanda Page outlined preliminary budget priorities including roughly 5% step and performance pay increases for all employees, additional street maintenance base funding, and up to $25 million in equitable and green infrastructure capital investments, while requesting a two-hour special session to prioritize Council's new budget requests. Council reviewed results from the annual resident survey (673 completed responses highlighting public schools, sidewalks, and transit priorities) and received an update on the City's strategic plan development. Afternoon deliberations focused on draft FY 2023-24 budget guidelines, potential revenue sources, maintaining fare-free transit service, and next steps ahead of budget adoption, with no formal votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Day 2 Opening and City Manager Preliminary Budget Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and Management Services staff welcomed Council back to the Water Management facility for Day 2 of the retreat. City Manager Wanda Page highlighted preliminary projections funding ~5% step and performance increases for all city employees, added street maintenance base funding, and up to $25 million for equitable and green infrastructure, and asked Council to schedule a two-hour special session to prioritize council budget requests.

agenda_items.title: Annual Resident Survey Presentation (ETC Institute)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and survey consultant Jason presented findings from 673 completed resident surveys exceeding the 600-response target. Key importance-satisfaction findings pointed to public schools, pedestrian sidewalks, and public transit systems as top resident priorities, alongside demographic breakdowns across Black, Hispanic, and white respondents.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Development Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed progress on drafting five to seven objectives per strategic goal area, incorporating resident and bilingual survey input alongside department business plans. Goals included delivering city services effectively, advancing the workforce, and building an innovative, high-performing organization.

agenda_items.title: FY 2023-24 Budget Guidelines, Revenue Options, and Fare-Free Transit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and budget staff reviewed draft budget guidelines language regarding new revenue sources, property tax capacity, council and staff budget requests, and sustaining fare-free transit service into FY 2023-24. City Manager Wanda Page and Council members closed the retreat by thanking staff for preparing projections amid high vacancy rates and confirming follow-up work sessions ahead of the May budget recommendation and June adoption.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat March 2, 2023 (live stream)

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Feb. 23, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 23, 2023 work session (with Mark-Anthony Middleton on excused absence and Leonardo Williams arriving shortly after roll call), the Durham City Council approved priority items from City Manager Wanda Page and City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg, voting 5-0 twice to accept the attorney's priority item and hold a closed session on threatened litigation. Council reviewed the March 6 agenda, with DeDreana Freeman pulling Item 4 (2022 boards and commissions attendance reports) to flag incomplete reporting and 0%–33% member attendance. In the afternoon, staff presented the FY 2022-23 Q2 financial report—prompting Freeman to ask about vacancy bonuses and municipal tax rebates—and unveiled the Aquatic Splash and Play final report proposing a neighborhood pool at East End Park and new amenities at the former Wheels site, which drew sharp critique from Freeman over committee communication before Council voted 6-0 to settle the March 6 agenda and adjourned to closed session.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Priority Items, and Closed Session Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Clerk Ashley Wyatt called the roll with five members present, Mark-Anthony Middleton on excused absence, and Leonardo Williams arriving shortly afterward at 00:10:14. City Manager Wanda Page added a presentation for Item 6 (2022 Q4 Crime Report), and City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg requested a closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding threatened litigation; Council voted 5-0 to accept the priority item and 5-0 to hold the closed session.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Reading and Pulled Item 4 (Boards & Commissions Attendance)

agenda_items.title: FY 2022-23 Second Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff concluded the Q2 financial briefing noting positive revenue/budget variances in Parking (+$309K revenue), DPAC (+$264K), and Inspections (+$160K revenue / +$272K positive variance from personnel savings), with Ballpark meeting projections. DeDreana Freeman asked the City Attorney to research municipal tax rebate models (citing Merriam, Kansas), urged converting vacancy savings into bonuses for overworked staff, and raised red flags over inspection and stormwater staffing shortages.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham Aquatic Splash and Play Final Report

meetings.title: Durham City Council Feb. 20, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 20, 2023 regular meeting (all seven members present), the Durham City Council recognized 96-year-old retired NCCU economics professor Dr. E. Victor Mafo, celebrated a $400,000 USDOT Safe Streets and Roads for All grant and 2022 Tree City USA designation, and voted 7-0 to grant Mark-Anthony Middleton an excused absence for the February 23 work session. City Manager Wanda Page presented priority item updates including moving the Support Youth Mentoring Services Act to fifth on the City's 2023 legislative agenda (Item 54). In public hearings, Council voted 7-0 to approve an RS-MD text-only rezoning capped at five townhouse units and 7-0 to approve Item 50, adding a Transitional Office Overlay at 1907 South Miami Boulevard for a substance-use counseling office despite church neighbor concerns about area crime. The meeting ended with sharp supplemental friction over council decorum and staff responsiveness to residents ahead of Thursday's Splash and Play work session presentation.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Ceremonial Recognitions, and Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal convened the meeting with all seven council members present, honored 96-year-old former NCCU economics professor Dr. E. Victor Mafo, and recognized Durham's $400,000 USDOT Safe Streets and Roads for All grant and 2022 Tree City USA award. Council approved 7-0 an excused absence for Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton to attend a February 23 NC League of Municipalities board meeting.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Consent Agenda Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page reported priority revisions for Item 25 (adding environmental services to on-call professional agreements), Item 26 (energy audit contract duplicate exhibit removal), Item 49 (revised development plan), and Item 54 (elevating the Support Youth Mentoring Services Act to priority #5 on the 2023 legislative agenda). Mayor O'Neal read the consent agenda including the parking audit, Hardy Street Apartments multifamily housing revenue bonds, Community Safety and Wellness Task Force annual report, fire pumper trucks, and Piney Wood Park pickleball court renovations.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - RS-10 to RS-MD (Maximum 5 Townhouse Units)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding over the hearing, Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton closed the public hearing with no additional non-applicant speakers. Council voted 7-0 to adopt the UDO amendment rezoning the parcel from RS-10 to RS-MD with a text-only development plan capped at five townhouse units, and 7-0 to adopt the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change - 1907 South Miami Boulevard (RS-20 to RS-20 TO)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Morningstar Law Group's general rezoning application to add a Transitional Office Overlay (TO) to a 0.178-acre RS-20 parcel at 1907 South Miami Boulevard for Mr. Dockery's DUI/substance-use counseling practice, which the Planning Commission endorsed 10-2. After DeDreana Freeman confirmed no statute bars such a facility near schools and neighbors from a nearby church raised crime concerns, Council praised Dockery's community work, lamented the cost of rezoning a single small property, and approved the ordinance and consistency statement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Remarks on Staff Responsiveness and Upcoming Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members exchanged pointed remarks after a two-minute public comment, debating perceived disregard by staff toward residents versus deferring substantive discussion to Thursday's work session presentation. Mayor O'Neal acknowledged speaking out of order while defending residents' right to voice concerns respectfully before adjourning at 10:26 PM.

meetings.executive_summary: At the February 9, 2023 work session (all seven members present), Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened with reflections on a campus incident at Hillside High School and secured unanimous thumbs-up consensus to reschedule the two-day Budget Retreat to March 2–3, while Mark-Anthony Middleton gained consensus to place a 911 telecommunicators 'First Responders Resolution' on the next work session agenda and Jillian Johnson gave notice of an expedited resolution opposing anti-LGBTQ+ state legislation. Later in the session, Don't Waste Durham and student researchers presented a proposed 10-cent plastic bag fee ordinance, sparking a policy split between Javiera Caballero (backing an ordinance with an 18-month timeline and bilingual outreach) and Leonardo Williams (favoring an education-first resolution over a fee), before Council voted 7-0 to settle the February 20 agenda and adjourned to closed session.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Hillside High Reflection, and Council Proposals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened the work session with reflections on Hillside High School, called the roll with all seven members present, urged colleagues to maintain public decorum, and received unanimous thumbs-up consensus to hold the Budget Retreat on March 2–3. disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Feb 9, 2023
disagreements.issue: Proposed 10-Cent Plastic Bag Fee Ordinance vs. Education-First Resolution
disagreements.summary: Following a presentation by Don't Waste Durham and university clinic researchers, council members divided over whether to advance an enforceable 10-cent plastic bag fee ordinance with a transition period or begin with a non-binding resolution and public education campaign.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support moving forward with a plastic bag fee ordinance paired with a clear timeline and bilingual public education campaign.
side_a_arguments: Pricing undesirable single-use items is a proven tool to drive both individual and collective behavior change.
An ordinance with an explicit transition timeline (such as 18 months) provides clarity while allowing thorough multilingual outreach.
Other jurisdictions worldwide—including countries with much lower average wealth—have successfully implemented plastic bag restrictions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support a robust public education campaign and resolution first, viewing a mandatory 10-cent fee ordinance as premature.
side_b_arguments: A 10-cent per-bag fee creates psychological and financial burdens on low-income residents who already pay more for healthy food.
Policing and enforcing local mandates proved challenging during the pandemic.
A robust education campaign coupled with a resolution can build public buy-in before considering an ordinance.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken at the work session; policy discussion left open for further council work.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Feb. 6, 2023 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 6, 2023 regular meeting (all seven members present), the Durham City Council honored the North Carolina Central University Eagles football team for winning the Celebration Bowl / HBCU National Championship and heard sharp council debate over policing and crisis response—with Jillian Johnson advocating a budget expansion of the HEART team to 24/7 citywide coverage following the Memphis police killing, Mark-Anthony Middleton rejecting comparisons between Durham PD and Memphis PD, and DeDreana Freeman seconding Middleton's call to bring Durham's Police Chief before Council. Later in the night, Council held a contentious deliberation over a ~420-home consolidated annexation and PDR 4.680 rezoning in the Falls/Jordan watershed (One More Carolinas LLC) after residents presented cloudy sink water and cited 'blood red' creek runoff. Over objections from Elaine O'Neal, DeDreana Freeman, and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman regarding unmitigated sediment runoff and pending county erosion amendments, Council approved the annexation and PDR 4.680 rezoning 4-3 and adopted the consistency statement 6-1.

agenda_items.title: Land Acknowledgment and NCCU Eagles Celebration Bowl Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened Eagle Night in Chambers, DeDreana Freeman read an indigenous land and labor acknowledgment, and Council honored Coach Trei Oliver and the NCCU Eagles football team for winning the Celebration Bowl and HBCU National Championship.

agenda_items.title: Debate on HEART 24/7 Budget Expansion and Policing Oversight
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jillian Johnson announced a budget request to expand the HEART crisis response team to 24/7 citywide service and referenced a rally with Durham Beyond Policing and the police killing in Memphis. Mark-Anthony Middleton pushed back forcefully against comparing Durham Police to Memphis PD and criticized targeting city staff rather than elected officials, while DeDreana Freeman highlighted the tasing death of Darryl Tyree Williams in Raleigh and seconded Middleton's request to have Durham's Police Chief address Council.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and PDR 4.680 Rezoning (One More Carolinas LLC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated a 420-home development proposal by One More Carolinas LLC in the Falls/Jordan District B watershed after residents displayed a bottle of turbid sink water and reported blood-red creek runoff near prior developments. Leonardo Williams argued opponents had not linked existing creek impairment to this project, while opposing members urged developers to proffer adherence to Durham County's pending sedimentation and erosion control amendments; Council passed the annexation and PDR 4.680 rezoning 4-3 and the consistency statement 6-1.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Annexation and rezoning passed 4-3; consistency statement passed 6-1

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement (One More Carolinas LLC)
votes.discussion_detail: Motion moved by Leonardo Williams and seconded by Mark-Anthony Middleton to adopt an ordinance annexing the property into the City of Durham effective March 31, 2023 and authorizing a utility extension agreement with One More Carolinas LLC. Passed 4-3 with Elaine O'Neal, DeDreana Freeman, and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman voting no.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change - RS-20 and CG to PDR 4.680 (One More Carolinas LLC)
votes.discussion_detail: Motion moved by Leonardo Williams and seconded by Jillian Johnson to adopt a UDO ordinance rezoning the property from RS-20 and CG (Falls/Jordan District B County jurisdiction) to Planned Development Residential 4.680 (PDR 4.680, Falls/Jordan District B City jurisdiction). Passed 4-3 with Elaine O'Neal, DeDreana Freeman, and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman voting no.

votes.item_title: NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement (One More Carolinas LLC)
votes.discussion_detail: Motion moved by Mark-Anthony Middleton and seconded by Leonardo Williams to adopt the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement. Passed 6-1 with Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman voting no.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Feb. 6, 2023 (Livestream)
disagreements.issue: HEART Team Expansion Framing and Comparisons Between Durham PD and Memphis PD
disagreements.summary: During council announcements, members clashed over how Durham's HEART alternative crisis response expansion and local policing oversight were framed in light of the police killing in Memphis and the tasing death of Darryl Tyree Williams in Raleigh.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advocate expanding the HEART crisis response program to 24/7 citywide coverage in the upcoming budget and highlight alternative response amid national scrutiny of policing.
side_a_arguments: HEART has demonstrated success and should be funded to operate 24/7 across the entire city.

Community rallies with Durham Beyond Policing underscore public demand for non-police crisis response, heightened by national attention following the police killing in Memphis where Durham's former chief serves.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject equating Durham Police Department with Memphis PD, oppose targeting city employees, and invite the Police Chief before Council to address regional incidents.
side_b_arguments: Durham Police Department is not the Memphis Police Department, and policy disputes should be directed at elected officials on the ballot rather than W-2 city employees.
Bringing Durham's Police Chief before Council allows members to ask direct questions about local practices following regional tragedies such as the tasing death of Darryl Tyree Williams in Raleigh.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; DeDreana Freeman seconded Mark-Anthony Middleton's request to bring the Police Chief before Council during the upcoming budget/oversight cycle.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Feb. 6, 2023 (Livestream)
disagreements.issue: One More Carolinas LLC Annexation and PDR 4.680 Rezoning Amid Creek Sediment Concerns
disagreements.summary: Council split 4-3 on annexing and rezoning land for roughly 420 homes in the Falls/Jordan District B watershed after residents presented turbid sink water and complained of blood-red creek runoff.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the annexation and PDR 4.680 rezoning to allow ~420 homes without delaying development over unverified causation claims.
side_a_arguments: The creek has been impaired historically, and opponents have not presented scientific evidence linking this project or recent development activity to increased impairment.
Blanket 'slow down building' arguments do not resolve technical jurisdictional responsibilities, which planning and county staff are working to clarify.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the annexation and rezoning until stronger sedimentation/erosion protections and resident water-quality concerns are addressed.
side_b_arguments: Residents cannot afford private laboratory testing for turbid sink water and blood-red creek runoff and should not have their concerns dismissed as antagonistic.
Council has repeatedly asked developers to proffer compliance with Durham County's stronger sedimentation and erosion control amendments before approval.
disagreements.resolution: Annexation and PDR 4.680 rezoning both passed 4-3; the statutory consistency statement subsequently passed 6-1 with Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman dissenting.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Jan. 19, 2023 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal presided over the January 19, 2023 Durham City Council work session, with Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton on excused absence at the U.S. Conference of Mayors in Washington, D.C. and Leonardo Williams arriving shortly after roll call. During announcements, Jillian Johnson requested consent to bring a draft single-use plastic bag ordinance from Don't Waste Durham to the February 9 work session, and council members recognized youth mentoring programs and the NCCU football team. Council heard public comments from J.J. Henderson Towers residents citing power outages, maintenance failures, and disability accommodation complaints, followed by two major presentations: the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement community violence intervention and mentoring pipeline led by DeDreana Freeman, and an Affordable Housing Deep Dive on the Durham Housing Authority (DHA) led by Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman. Council settled the upcoming regular meeting agenda by a unanimous 6-0 voice vote and promoted the January 25 Point-in-Time homelessness count before adjourning at 3:46 PM.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal called the work session to order, noted Mark-Anthony Middleton's excused absence for the U.S. Conference of Mayors, and noted Leonardo Williams was en route. Jillian Johnson requested colleague permission to invite Don't Waste Durham to present a draft ordinance limiting single-use plastic bags at the February 9 work session. Other council announcements highlighted Durham youth mentoring finalists honored at the Governor's Mansion, an evening ceremony honoring over 54 mentoring programs, and recognition for the NCCU football team.

agenda_items.title: Draft Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal read the draft agenda items, including Public Works pavement management services (Item 4, ST-327C), a Solid Waste contract amendment with Rubicon Global LLC for in-vehicle technology (Item 5), and a Water Management waterline replacement contract on Old Chapel Hill Road at New Hope Creek (Item 6). She also noted presentations on the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement (Item 7) and Durham Housing Authority (Item 8), plus five planning public hearings covering consolidated annexations and UDO text/development plan revisions (Items 9-13).

agenda_items.title: J.J. Henderson Towers Resident Concerns and Property Management Complaints
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Javiera Caballero managed Citizens' Matters cards as residents raised urgent housing and maintenance complaints. Speakers including Hurley Williams (807 South Duke Street, former J.J. Henderson Towers tenant vice president) described power outages without notice, conditions during December 23-24, dissatisfaction with CCI property management, and demands for reasonable disability accommodations alongside correspondence to HUD.

agenda_items.title: Hayti Reborn Justice Movement Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Led by DeDreana Freeman, former Police Chief Steve Chalmers and community partners presented the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement's collaborative violence-reduction and support pipeline. Presenters emphasized channeling funding to community-based partner organizations rather than competing for the same dollars, pairing participants with mentors, and providing education and life preparation. Freeman noted she brought the update to the public work session as a transparent follow-up to initial discussions dating back to 2021.

agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Deep Dive: Durham Housing Authority (Q&A Excerpt)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Led by Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman, Council continued its deep dive with Durham Housing Authority leadership regarding staffing shortages that prevent DHA from taking over property management from private partners despite contractual takeover clauses. Members discussed mixed-income communities, voucher discrimination by landlords, and the budget trade-off in which raising Fair Market Rents improves unit quality but reduces the number of vouchers DHA can fund. Council members expressed contrasting views on public housing's viability, with some emphasizing mixed-income redevelopment while others defended fully government-funded public housing as a human right.

agenda_items.title: Settling the Regular City Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page presented the recommended agenda placement of Items 1-6 on the Consent Agenda and Items 9-13 on the General Business Agenda for public hearings. Leonardo Williams moved and Javiera Caballero seconded settling the agenda as presented.

agenda_items.title: 2023 Point-in-Time Homelessness Count and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal urged residents to volunteer for Durham's 2023 Point-in-Time (PIT) homelessness count on January 25, 2023 from 7:30 PM to 11:30 PM, organized by Housing for New Hope out of the Durham County Main Library auditorium with winter supply bags and trained teams. Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman added that 90 of her graduating MSW leadership students would participate before the meeting adjourned at 3:46 PM.

votes.item_title: Settle the Regular City Council Agenda (Consent Items 1-6; General Business Public Hearings Items 9-13)
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton was on an excused absence at the U.S. Conference of Mayors in Washington, D.C.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Wanda Page recommended placing Items 1-6 on the Consent Agenda and Items 9-13 on the General Business Agenda for public hearings. Leonardo Williams moved approval and Javiera Caballero seconded. Mayor Elaine O'Neal called for a verbal vote of aye; hearing no opposition, she declared the motion passed.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Jan. 19, 2023 (Livestream)
disagreements.issue: Role of Public Housing vs. Mixed-Income Private-Market Partnerships
disagreements.summary: During the Durham Housing Authority deep-dive discussion, council members diverged on whether concentrated public housing is a failed model that must shift toward mixed-income communities or whether government-funded public housing must be championed as a guaranteed human right.
disagreements.side_a_position: Shift away from concentrated public housing toward structured mixed-income communities that integrate residents socioeconomically rather than isolating low-income households.
side_a_arguments: Concentrated public housing can trap residents in environments with maintenance failures and crime.
Mixed-income communities create better-run, welcoming environments that encourage upward mobility and integration into Durham.
disagreements.side_b_position: Government-funded public housing is 100% the solution and housing must be treated and funded as a guaranteed human right rather than left to a capitalist market.
side_b_arguments: Public housing only struggles when the federal government underfunds it, unlike systems in Western Europe where government investment keeps housing affordable.
Treating housing purely as a market commodity guarantees displacement and homelessness for residents who cannot pay market rates.
disagreements.resolution: Informational discussion only; no vote taken. (Individual speaker turns in this portion of the digest were not verbally named on the audio except Mayor O'Neal noting prior remarks by Jillian Johnson and Javiera Caballero before the exchange.)

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan. 17, 2023 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton presided over the January 17, 2023 Durham City Council regular meeting while Mayor Elaine O'Neal traveled to Washington, D.C. for the U.S. Conference of Mayors. Council heard a Year of the Trail proclamation led by Javiera Caballero, Leonardo Williams' announcement of a planned task force on Black men and boys, and unanimously approved three excused absences for O'Neal, Jillian Johnson (March 6 and 9), and Middleton (January 19 work session). Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript covering the consent agenda and earlier hearings, Council engaged in a contentious debate over the Kemp Road Residential consolidated annexation and Utility Extension Agreement with Bethesda Association LLC. Despite Middleton's defense of the project and developer proffers tying building permits to Fire Station 21, Council rejected the annexation and UEA 2-4, with DeDreana Freeman, Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman, Jillian Johnson, and Javiera Caballero voting no, eliminating jurisdiction for subsequent rezoning motions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, Pledge, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton called the meeting to order at 7:00 PM and explained that Mayor Elaine O'Neal was en route to the U.S. Conference of Mayors in Washington, D.C., with Middleton slated to join her for the second half of the conference. Following silent meditation and the Pledge of Allegiance led by DeDreana Freeman, roll call noted O'Neal's requested excused absence and that Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman was delayed.

agenda_items.title: Year of the Trail Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Javiera Caballero read a proclamation recognizing 2023 as North Carolina's Year of the Trail alongside Durham Parks and Recreation staff including Ms. Morales. The proclamation highlighted Durham's greenway system, connections to the East Coast Greenway and Mountains-to-Sea Trail, climate resilience benefits, and Parks and Recreation trail programs.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, City Manager/Attorney Priority Items, and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jillian Johnson requested excused absences for March 6 and March 9 due to international travel, and Leonardo Williams announced plans to propose a budget-season task force studying criminal justice and academic disparities facing Black men and boys in Durham. City Manager Wanda Page reported one priority item adding information to the upcoming Homeless Continuum of Care deep-dive presentation, and City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg had no priority items. Council then approved excused absences for Elaine O'Neal, Jillian Johnson, and Mark-Anthony Middleton in three unanimous votes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton read the Consent Agenda into the record, including a resolution supporting ICAN's Cities Appeal for the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (Item 1), ARPA funding for Family Child Care Homes, Reentry Housing Support, and Transitional and Independent Housing (Items 2-4), a Context Systems audiovisual contract amendment (Item 5), a Made in Durham contract (Item 6), and an interlocal agreement amendment for a transit plan governance study (Item 7). Consent action and interim items occur in the truncated middle section of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Kemp Road Residential Consolidated Annexation and Utility Extension Agreement (Bethesda Association LLC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated annexing and extending utilities for the Kemp Road Residential project east of Kemp Road, with opponents citing draft staff growth-management guidance advising against development east of Kemp Road until fire and infrastructure capacity are in place, questioning 600-foot resident mail notifications and an unsuccessful fire station site offer, and warning of a domino effect similar to prior Olive Branch Road rezonings. The applicant committed not to apply for a building permit until a building permit is filed for Fire Station 21, and Fire Department staff noted Station 8 and Station 17 could respond via mutual aid in roughly four to five minutes. Mark-Anthony Middleton defended the project against developer-influence accusations and argued Durham cannot impose a development moratorium, but the annexation motion failed 2-4, leaving Council without jurisdiction to vote on the rezoning or consistency statement.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence to Mayor Elaine O'Neal (Jan. 17, 2023)
votes.notes: Elaine O'Neal was absent; Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman was noted as delayed at roll call (00:04:15) and is omitted from confirmed ayes on early procedural votes.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton entertained a motion to excuse Mayor Elaine O'Neal's absence while traveling to the U.S. Conference of Mayors. Leonardo Williams moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded; the clerk reported the motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absences to Council Member Jillian Johnson (March 6 & March 9, 2023)
votes.notes: Elaine O'Neal was absent; Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman was noted as delayed at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Jillian Johnson's announcement of planned international travel, Leonardo Williams moved and Javiera Caballero seconded granting her excused absences for the March 6 regular council meeting and March 9 work session. The clerk reported the motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Grant Excused Absence to Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton (Jan. 19, 2023 Work Session)
votes.notes: Elaine O'Neal was absent; Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman was noted as delayed at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton requested an excused absence for the January 19 work session so he could represent Durham during the second half of the U.S. Conference of Mayors in Washington, D.C. Leonardo Williams moved and Jillian Johnson seconded; the clerk reported the motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adopt Ordinance Annexing Kemp Road Residential and Authorizing Utility Extension Agreement with Bethesda Association LLC
votes.notes: Transcript ASR renders 'Kemp Road' as 'Kimb Road'. Elaine O'Neal had an excused absence; the 2 ayes correspond to the remaining seated members present (Mark-Anthony Middleton and Leonardo Williams).
votes.discussion_detail: After extended debate over draft growth boundaries east of Kemp Road, fire service coverage, and resident notifications, Leonardo Williams moved and Jillian Johnson seconded the annexation and utility extension agreement with Bethesda Association LLC. The clerk closed the vote and reported the motion failed 4-2 (2 ayes, 4 nays), with DeDreana Freeman, Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman, Jillian Johnson, and Javiera Caballero voting no. City Attorney advice confirmed no jurisdiction remained for the rezoning or consistency statement motions.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Jan. 17, 2023 (Livestream)
disagreements.issue: Kemp Road Residential Annexation East of Draft Infrastructure Growth Boundary
disagreements.summary: Council split 2-4 over whether to approve a consolidated annexation and utility extension agreement east of Kemp Road ahead of finalized Comprehensive Plan/infrastructure rules and Fire Station 21 construction.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the annexation and utility extension agreement based on its project merits and fire-permit condition rather than uncodified draft policy lines.
side_a_arguments: The draft growth-boundary guidance is not yet codified law and Council should not cede decision-making to draft staff proposals.
Durham cannot legally enact a development moratorium and is one of the fastest-growing cities in the country.
The developer proffered not to seek building permits until Fire Station 21 permits are applied for, and Stations 8 and 17 are within 4-5 minutes via mutual aid.
Opposing growth under slogans like 'preserve rural Durham' can function as coded resistance to urbanization, and supporters should not be accused of being in developers' pockets.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject annexation east of Kemp Road until municipal infrastructure, fire coverage, and adopted growth policies are in place.
side_b_arguments: Planning staff are neutral arbiters whose guidance advises against building east of Kemp Road until infrastructure capacity improves.
Approving one project across the line creates a domino effect into unready areas, repeating past 4-3 Olive Branch Road rezoning controversies.
Concerns remained over 600-foot resident notification delivery and an earlier proposed fire station site across a stream that proved unviable.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to annex and authorize the Utility Extension Agreement failed 2-4 at 03:19:37, rendering the companion rezoning and consistency motions without jurisdiction.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Jan. 5, 2023 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal presided over the January 5, 2023 Durham City Council work session, with Javiera Caballero on excused absence and DeDreana Freeman and Leonardo Williams arriving after roll call. Council unanimously approved City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg's priority item to hold a closed session at the end of the meeting regarding Fourth Circuit litigation (Plaintiff Parent v. City of Durham). After hearing public comments on a dedicated Duke-to-UNC bicycle path, Wellons Village gun violence and ShotSpotter funding, and fire/EMS coverage for new developments, Council heard two deep-dive briefings: the Durham Homeless Continuum of Care (led by Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman) and the DCHC MPO FY 2021-22 Annual Report (led by Mark-Anthony Middleton). Council then voted unanimously to settle the January 17 regular meeting agenda before adjourning into closed session at 3:08 PM.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and City Attorney Closed Session Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened the work session, noting Javiera Caballero's excused absence and delayed arrivals for DeDreana Freeman and Leonardo Williams. City Manager Wanda Page and the City Clerk had no priority items, while City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg requested a closed session at the conclusion of business under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation on Plaintiff Parent v. City of Durham, Michelle Susie Scott, Pinnacle in the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals. Council unanimously approved accepting the priority item and holding the closed session.

agenda_items.title: Draft Agenda Reading and Pulled Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor O'Neal read the draft agenda covering an ICAN nuclear weapons treaty resolution (Item 1), ARPA grants for family child care, reentry housing, and transitional housing (Items 2-4), a broadcasting support contract amendment (Item 5), a Made in Durham contract (Item 6, pulled by DeDreana Freeman), a transit governance study ILA amendment (Item 7), presentations (Items 8-9), and four planning public hearings (Items 10-13). A council member thanked staff, the Biden administration, and Congressional Democrats for moving ARPA funding rapidly to the community.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Duke-UNC Bike Path, Wellons Village Safety, and Development Infrastructure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Phil Reamer urged Durham to prioritize long-haul 8-to-10-mile separated bikeways—specifically a dedicated bicycle path between Duke University and UNC-Chapel Hill—rather than short painted lanes along high-speed roads. John Tate Dunston addressed New Year's Day shootings in Wellons Village, arguing ShotSpotter funds should instead pay for four additional police officers to patrol neighborhoods. Another speaker (preceding a truncated middle section) raised concerns about developments lacking existing fire/EMS coverage and urged stronger developer proffers ahead of January 17 hearings.

agenda_items.title: Affordable Housing Deep Dive: Durham Homeless Continuum of Care
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Led by Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman, Continuum of Care staff (including Mr. Davis) reviewed federal HUD homelessness prioritization tiers and explained that federal rules require rental assistance payments go to third-party landlords and utilities rather than direct stipends favored by DeDreana Freeman. Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton praised Durham's ~$2 million dedicated housing penny investment and announced plans to propose extending and expanding Durham's guaranteed income pilot during the upcoming budget cycle. Mayor Elaine O'Neal requested the CoC's top three legislative and budget needs for the next 12 months.

agenda_items.title: DCHC MPO FY 2021-22 Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Led by Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton, DCHC MPO Executive Director Doug Placzynski presented the MPO's annual report, highlighting Vision Zero safety work, upgraded public involvement policies, and repositioning the MPO to Triangle J Council of Governments (TJCOG). Placzynski projected a 10-15% increase in local match dues—roughly $30,000-$40,000 more for Durham above its current ~$1-per-resident contribution toward the $5.5 million MPO budget—to free City Transportation staff to focus on delivering local projects.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Jan. 3, 2023 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal presided over the first Durham City Council meeting of 2023 on January 3, with six members present and Javiera Caballero on an excused absence. Ceremonial recognitions included proclaiming January 2023 as Courage Month and reading two National Mentoring Month proclamations, alongside remarks by DeDreana Freeman urging community-level intervention to protect youth before law enforcement involvement. Council unanimously passed the Consent Agenda (Items 1-7) by a 6-0 show of hands, heard the staff presentation on Welcome Venture Park (Item 9, with Mark-Anthony Middleton disclosing a non-financial notification-area relationship), and unanimously approved (6-0) the Aura Hillandale West rezoning to Planned Development Residential 59.102 after neighborhood discussion of tree preservation and sidewalk alignment. Council also unanimously approved (6-0) the Chapel Hill Road convenience store rezoning to Commercial Neighborhood before adjourning at 8:23 PM.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Courage Month, and National Mentoring Month Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened the meeting with silent meditation, DeDreana Freeman led the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call recorded six members present with Javiera Caballero excused. O'Neal proclaimed January 2023 as Courage Month, and council presented two National Mentoring Month proclamations recognizing local youth programs including D.F. Forbes Youth Foundation, Durham Proud, 100 Black Men of Triangle East, Bull City Bulldogs, We Are Kings, and We Are Queens. Freeman urged residents to engage directly with neighborhood youth to prevent violence before police or news cameras arrive.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Updates and Consent Agenda Approval (Items 1-7)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page reported revised development plans and proffers for Item 9 (Welcome Venture Park) and Item 10 (Aura Hillandale West), while the City Attorney and City Clerk had no priority items. Mayor O'Neal read Consent Agenda Items 1-7, including board appointments, the November 2022 bid report, permit fee reimbursement for disabled veteran housing construction, ARPA Multifamily Acquisition Support, a wireless lease at 1318 East Pettigrew Street, and a John R. McAdams contract. Council approved the Consent Agenda unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Welcome Venture Park Zoning Map Change
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton opened the Item 9 public hearing and disclosed for transparency that an organization where he serves as a principal is a major landowner within the notification area without any financial conflict. Planner Brooke Roper reported the Planning Commission recommended approval 11-0 for Industrial Light with a development plan consistent with the Future Land Use Map, requiring three motions. The applicant's presentation and vote occur within the truncated middle section of the transcript.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval: Aura Hillandale West Zoning Map Change (PDR 59.102)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the Aura Hillandale West request to rezone property from Industrial Light to Planned Development Residential 59.102 alongside a Future Land Use Map change to High Density Residential and Recreation & Open Space, noting an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation on October 11, 2022. Seven proponents signed up and nearby residents including Julie Mancuso Craig and Karen Cantor addressed the project, with speakers urging preservation of existing trees by combining city and developer sidewalks. Staff noted forestry staff work to minimize root impacts and the applicant noted neighborhood-agreed replacement plantings, after which Council unanimously approved all three required motions.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval: Chapel Hill Road Convenience Store Zoning Map Change
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Led by Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton, planner Brooke Roper presented Christopher Kowski's request for 0.2 acres at 2945 Chapel Hill Road and 3036 University Drive to rezone from RS-8 and RS-10 to Commercial Neighborhood with a text-only development plan to reconstruct the existing convenience store. No members of the public spoke on the item, and Council unanimously passed both the zoning ordinance and consistency statement motions.

agenda_items.title: Hayti Reborn Work Session Scheduling and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DeDreana Freeman confirmed scheduling the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement presentation for the January 19 work session and clarified it did not concern Fayette Place. Mayor O'Neal closed with remarks honoring Courage Month, victims of shootings, and longtime resident Anita Green's admonition to 'be a kind human being' before adjourning at 8:23 PM.

votes.item_title: Authorize City Manager to Enter Utility Extension Agreement with Trinsic Acquisition Company LLC (Aura Hillandale West)
votes.notes: Javiera Caballero had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing on Item 10 (Aura Hillandale West), Leonardo Williams moved and Mayor Elaine O'Neal seconded authorizing the City Manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with Trinsic Acquisition Company LLC. After resolving a brief electronic voting system hiccup, the chair announced the motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Ordinance Amending UDO for Aura Hillandale West (IL to PDR 59.102)
votes.notes: Javiera Caballero had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Leonardo Williams moved and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman seconded the zoning ordinance taking the Aura Hillandale West property out of Industrial Light (IL) and establishing Planned Development Residential 59.102 (PDR 59.102). The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Aura Hillandale West (NCGS 160D-605)
votes.notes: Javiera Caballero had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Leonardo Williams moved and Mayor Elaine O'Neal seconded adopting the statutory consistency statement under NCGS 160D-605 for Aura Hillandale West, accompanying the Future Land Use Map amendment to High Density Residential and Recreation & Open Space. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adopt Zoning Ordinance for Chapel Hill Road Convenience Store (RS-8 & RS-10 to Commercial Neighborhood Text-Only Development Plan)
votes.notes: Javiera Caballero had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the public hearing on Item 11 (2945 Chapel Hill Road and 3036 University Drive) with no public opposition, Leonardo Williams moved and Mayor Elaine O'Neal seconded rezoning the 0.2-acre site from RS-8 and RS-10 to Commercial Neighborhood with a text-only development plan. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adopt Consistency Statement for Chapel Hill Road Convenience Store (NCGS 160D-605)
votes.notes: Javiera Caballero had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Leonardo Williams moved and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman seconded adopting the consistency statement required under NCGS 160D-605 for the Chapel Hill Road convenience store rezoning and Commercial Future Land Use Map amendment. The motion passed unanimously.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 20, 2022 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 20, 2022 work session—the final meeting of the year—Council Member Jillian Johnson highlighted completion progress at Durham Housing Authority's 'The Joyce' senior affordable housing development and pulled Consent Item 4 to explore expanding permit fee reimbursements beyond disabled veterans to other vulnerable groups. The session's centerpiece was an extended work-session discussion on disposition and redevelopment priorities for the city-owned 505 West Chapel Hill Street site, examining weak downtown hotel market indicators, high rehabilitation estimates for the historic Milton Small building, and trade-offs between affordable housing, destination/event space, commercial revenue, and public-private or county partnerships. Staff committed to returning in early 2023 with a formal disposition strategy and timeline for Council approval prior to issuing a new RFQ/RFP. Council also heard board and commission nominations and unanimously settled the January 3, 2023 regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Condolences, Housing Progress Remarks, and Consent Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal called the work session to order with six members present and Leonardo Williams arriving later, offering condolences for the passing of John Berness. Jillian Johnson celebrated imminent move-ins at Durham Housing Authority's senior development 'The Joyce,' and Mayor O'Neal read Consent Items 1–7, with Johnson pulling Item 4 (permit fee reimbursement for disabled veterans) and Javiera Caballero praising it.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Affordable Housing Assistance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident addressed Council regarding community needs and efforts to help individuals access affordable housing and maintenance assistance.

agenda_items.title: Permit Fee Reimbursement Program for Housing Construction for Disabled Veterans
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jillian Johnson pulled Item 4 to ask whether the administration was considering expanding permit fee reimbursements to other vulnerable populations, echoing earlier praise from Javiera Caballero. Staff explained the Inspections Department developed the item with Deputy City Manager Chadwell and had no additional proposals underway yet, though they were open to future ideas.

agenda_items.title: Disposition and Redevelopment Priorities for 505 West Chapel Hill Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and a development consultant reviewed prior RFP priorities for 505 West Chapel Hill Street (including 80 permanently affordable units at 60% AMI, land-sale/tax revenue, 250,000+ sq. ft. commercial space, and preserving the Milton Small building) alongside market data showing declining downtown hotel metrics and high historic rehab costs. Council members broadly affirmed affordable housing across income tiers as the top priority, with DeDreana Freeman proposing separating the Milton Small parcel and leasing rather than selling the rest, Leonardo Williams and Mark-Anthony Middleton advocating a destination/event space and private or county partnerships to offset preservation costs, and Jillian Johnson opposing an unrestricted sale. Staff stated they would return in the new year with a disposition strategy and timeline for Council approval.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations and Setting January 3, 2023 Council Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk announced nominations for the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (Maureen Quinlan for Ward 1, Peter Whitehead for Ward 2) and the Mayor's Hispanic/Latino Committee (Alejandra Montoya). The City Manager presented the January 3, 2023 agenda (Consent Items 1–7 and GBA Public Hearings Items 9–11), which Council approved unanimously before adjourning at 2:26 PM.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec. 19, 2022 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: The December 19, 2022 regular meeting opened with Mayor Elaine O'Neal presenting former Duke basketball coach Mike Krzyzewski ('Coach K') with a Key to the City and proclamation alongside Consent Item 9 designating part of NC-751/Cameron Boulevard as Coach K Highway. Due to a malfunctioning electronic voting board, Council conducted all votes by voice and hand vote, unanimously passing the Consent Agenda (including multiple ARPA housing and business equity projects and pipeline repair contracts) as well as zoning map changes for 4150 Old Chapel Hill Road (Item 20) and the Geer Junction consolidated annexation and rezoning (Item 21). Item 19 (Stella View consolidated annexation) was also heard, though its vote outcome is omitted from the truncated middle of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Coach K Key to the City Proclamation and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal presented a proclamation and Key to the City honoring Coach Mike Krzyzewski. During announcements, Mark-Anthony Middleton praised Oxford Manor residents' policy advocacy, congratulated North Carolina Central University on its victory, and noted Durham was simultaneously operating a guaranteed income pilot, HEART mental health responders, expanded violence interruption, and gunshot detection technology.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval Including ARPA Programs, Coach K Highway, and Utility Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page noted revised Fire Department fiscal impact analyses for Items 19 and 21 and supplemental ARPA Item 23 (Bridging Business Opportunity and Equity), while the City Clerk announced the voting board malfunctioned and requested hand votes. Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton read the consent agenda—covering board appointments, ARPA housing and resiliency funds, Coach K Highway resolution, Housing for New Hope landlord engagement, a hazard mitigation grant ordinance, and FY23 pipeline repair contracts—and Council approved it unanimously with no items pulled.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Stella View (1001, 1011, and 1031 Sharon Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young introduced a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial zoning request from Jeremy Anderson for three parcels totaling 62.75 acres at 1001, 1011, and 1031 Sharon Road. The remainder of the public hearing and any resulting vote occurred within a truncated portion of the transcript digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Transcript digest truncated; vote not shown

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 4150 Old Chapel Hill Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Applicant representative Patrick Byker presented on behalf of M.M. Fowler for 2.23 acres at Garrett Road and Old Chapel Hill Road, seeking Commercial General with a text-only development plan (CG(D)) prohibiting intensive uses and noting a 50-foot 80% opacity buffer and 9-2 Planning Commission recommendation. After closing the public hearing with no opposition speakers shown, Council unanimously adopted both the rezoning ordinance and the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Geer Junction (2240 and 3300 East Geer Street)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young presented a utility extension agreement, non-contiguous voluntary annexation, and rezoning to PDR 19.520 for 8.197 acres requested by Jared Edens of Edens Land Corp, alongside a recommended future land use map change to medium-high density residential. Opponent Jason Bizdula raised concerns over EMS, school, and road capacity; Transportation and City Manager Wanda Page responded regarding cumulative impact tracking in CIP and operating budgets, and Council unanimously approved all three required motions.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Zoning Map Change (4150 Old Chapel Hill Road) — UDO Amendment to CG(D)
votes.notes: Hand vote due to malfunctioning voting board; ruled unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted an ordinance amending the UDO by taking property out of Commercial Neighborhood (CN) and RS-20 and establishing Commercial General with a text-only development plan (CG(D)) prohibiting specified uses including agricultural uses, passenger terminals, social services, institutions, places of worship, major utilities, indoor firing ranges, commercial parking, and manufactured home sites.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Zoning Map Change (4150 Old Chapel Hill Road) — Consistency Statement (NCGS 160D-605)
votes.notes: Hand vote due to malfunctioning voting board; ruled unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the consistency statement required by NCGS 160D-605 for 4150 Old Chapel Hill Road.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Consolidated Annexation (Geer Junction) — Annexation Ordinance & Utility Extension Agreement
votes.notes: Hand vote due to malfunctioning voting board; ruled unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted an ordinance annexing Geer Junction (2240 and 3300 East Geer Street) effective December 31, 2022, and authorizing the City Manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with Edens Land Corp.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Consolidated Annexation (Geer Junction) — UDO Amendment to PDR 19.520
votes.notes: Hand vote due to malfunctioning voting board; ruled unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted an ordinance amending the UDO to rezone the property from Rural Residential (RR) Falls/Jordan District B (F/J-B) Major Transportation Corridor I-85 (MTC I-85) county jurisdiction to Planned Development Residential 19.520 (PDR 19.520) city jurisdiction.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Consolidated Annexation (Geer Junction) — Consistency Statement (NCGS 160D-605)
votes.notes: Hand vote due to malfunctioning voting board; ruled unanimous.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the consistency statement required by NCGS 160D-605 for Geer Junction.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 8, 2022 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton and Council Member Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman absent on excused travel, Mayor Elaine O'Neal led the December 8, 2022 work session, praising Durham's Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) for training 1,234 first responders while Jillian Johnson proposed bringing a resolution supporting the LGBTQ community. During Citizen Matters, Ardmore Drive residents Isaac Woods and Isaac Woods Jr. protested decades of lacking city water, sewer, paved streets, and fire hydrants despite 1987 annexation. Council heard a transit presentation from Transportation Director Shawn Egan—who apologized for directive language in a prior memo—and reviewed proposed development mitigation measures including 500-foot well testing near blasting, 50-acre mass-grading phase caps, and DEQ-approved flocculants, before settling the December 19 agenda and tapping Leonardo Williams to coordinate a joint meeting with the Planning Commission.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, LGBTQ Support Resolution Proposal, CIT Recognition, and Agenda Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Five council members answered roll call (Mark-Anthony Middleton and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman had excused absences, and Jillian Johnson planned to leave early). Johnson sought colleague consent to bring a resolution supporting the LGBTQ community, Mayor O'Neal recognized Durham's CIT program for training 1,234 first responders and reflected on her trip to Selma, Alabama, and O'Neal read Items 1–21 into the record, noting Item 3 (RDU mayoral appointment) was referred back to staff.

agenda_items.title: Ardmore Drive Water, Sewer, Stormwater, and Fire Protection Concerns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents Isaac Woods and Isaac Woods Jr. (705 Ardmore Drive) testified that Ardmore Drive still lacked city water, fire hydrants, sewer, stormwater drainage, and paved streets despite forced annexation in 1987 and ongoing city tax and stormwater fee payments. They urged Council to prioritize Ardmore Drive on city water and paving lists and cited UN General Assembly Resolution 64/292 on the human right to water and sanitation.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Better Bus Project Update and Durham County Transit Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Shawn Egan opened the transit presentations by apologizing to Council for statements in his memorandum that overstepped his advisory role while trying to convey riders' experiences. The remainder of the transit presentations occurred within a truncated portion of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Development Concerns and Mitigation Steps (Blasting, Mass Grading, and Runoff)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fire Marshal Moore and Planning staff detailed enforcement and proposed ordinance updates addressing development impacts, including well-water testing within 500 feet of blasting, potential local blasting ordinance and Building Code Council changes, continued Lick Creek monitoring, requiring DEQ-approved flocculants, and capping mass-grading phases at 50 acres (estimated to add $15,000–$20,000 per lot). Council members questioned cost impacts, compact land-disturbance effects, and Fire Marshal Moore's reference to unfounded claims.

agenda_items.title: Setting December 19 Agenda, National Mentoring Month, and Joint Planning Commission Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved settling the December 19 agenda (Consent Items 1–15 and GBA Public Hearings Items 19–21). Javiera Caballero briefed Council on Dr. Holsey-Hyman's National Mentoring Month resolution and event funding request, and Leonardo Williams reported informal majority support for a special joint meeting with the Planning Commission, which Mayor O'Neal asked Williams to coordinate with the City Clerk before adjourning at 3:43 PM.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for the December 19, 2022 Regular City Council Meeting (Consent: 1–15; GBA Public Hearings: 19–21)
votes.notes: Mark-Anthony Middleton and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman had excused absences; Jillian Johnson was announced at 00:02:23 as leaving early and is not heard after opening remarks, so the exact headcount at 02:41:09 is not read aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Council voted unanimously by voice vote to settle the December 19, 2022 regular meeting agenda.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec. 5, 2022 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: With both Mayor Elaine O'Neal and Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton on excused travel, Council Member Jillian Johnson presided over the December 5, 2022 regular meeting with five members present. Council passed the Consent Agenda 5-0—including the FY22 financial audit, Durham Fire Department response times audit, FY23–24 budget schedule, Durham Station Transit Center pre-construction and design contracts, Q3 crime report, street/bridge contracts, and last-mile fiber projects—after the City Manager noted revisions removing Durham Beyond Policing from Item 6, redirecting funds language from street contracts, and referring Items 8 and 28 back to staff. Council continued two rezoning/annexation public hearings (including Crescent Towns to January 17, 2023) and voted 5-0 to approve permanent street closures for Fontanelle Street and a portion of Gilbert Street, followed by discussion of hosting a joint meeting with the Planning Commission.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Announcements, and City Manager Priority Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jillian Johnson presided with five members present (Elaine O'Neal and Mark-Anthony Middleton had excused absences), offering support for Moore County residents facing power outages while Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman acknowledged World AIDS Day, International Children's Day, and budget staff's participatory budgeting outreach. The City Manager reported priority revisions removing Durham Beyond Policing from Item 6 (TCF / 'We Are the Ones'), replacing 'City Manager' with 'City Council' and removing 'redirecting funds' on road contracts 14–16 and 18, and referring Items 8 and 28 back to staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval: Audits, Transit Center Contracts, Crime Report, Street Paving, and Fiber
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jillian Johnson read Consent Items 1–5, 7, and 9–23, covering the FY22 ACFR, Fire Department response times audit, FY23–24 budget schedule, DPS PAL agreement, Durham Station Transit Center contracts with Samet-WC Construction JV and Perkins & Will, DOL WIOA grant amendment, 2022 Q3 crime report, street/bridge contracts, DPD digital evidence enhancements, and three last-mile fiber contracts. Council approved the consent agenda 5-0, and staff clarified to Leonardo Williams that the street projects were CIP-funded while the city actively sought federal Bipartisan Infrastructure Law grants.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Continuance Request to February 6, 2023
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the digest, applicant counsel Mr. Ghosh requested continuing an open public hearing to February 6, 2023 while an engineering consultant evaluated a commitment. Planning Director Sara Young confirmed schedule flexibility, and Council gave informal consensus to hold the public hearing open until February 6, 2023 without a formal vote.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Crescent Towns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Brooke Roper presented Tri Pointe Homes' consolidated annexation and Residential Compact District rezoning for a 102-unit project (reduced from 103) designated Design District on the future land use map. Following questions from Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman on open space and unit counts and a continuance request by applicant counsel Nil Ghosh, Council agreed by consensus to hold the public hearing open until January 17, 2023.

agenda_items.title: Permanent Closing of Fontanelle Street (Case SC2200003)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented a request by Pete Gitto (PGG Holdings LLC) to permanently close the entire 143-foot Fontanelle Street between Castle Bay Road and Fidelity Drive to recombine with 1100 and 1200 Castle Bay Road. With no public speakers, Council voted 5-0 to approve the street closure.

agenda_items.title: Permanent Closing of a Portion of Gilbert Street (Case SC2200005)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Triangle Mobile Storage LLC's request to permanently close 361.37 linear feet of Gilbert Street parallel to Holloway Street between North Alston Avenue and Calvin Street. DeDreana Freeman pressed staff to ensure close review of impacts near East Durham Park and Long Meadow Park trails despite Parks and Recreation offering no comments, before Council voted 5-0 to approve the closure.

agenda_items.title: Proposal for Joint City Council and Planning Commission Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Leonardo Williams proposed convening a dedicated joint meeting between City Council and the Planning Commission to align perspectives on land use cases. DeDreana Freeman suggested utilizing the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) or attending Planning Commission meetings to hear resident feedback, while Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman backed Williams's proposal for a joint convening before adjournment at 8:00 PM.

votes.item_title: Item 29: Permanent Closing of Fontanelle Street (SC2200003)
votes.notes: Elaine O'Neal and Mark-Anthony Middleton absent (excused).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the permanent closure of 143 feet of Fontanelle Street between Castle Bay Road and Fidelity Drive.

votes.item_title: Item 30: Permanent Closing of a Portion of Gilbert Street (SC2200005)

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Nov. 22, 2022 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 22, 2022 work session with all seven members present, Council unanimously approved Javiera Caballero's excused absence request for January 3 and 5, 2023, and voted unanimously to hold a closed session at the end of regular business regarding the federal litigation Willie Womble v. City of Durham. Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton read the agenda and celebrated a >$10 million FTA grant for Durham Transit Center design (Item 10), while council members pulled multiple items including the Triangle Community Foundation / 'We Are the Ones' contract (Item 6), DPS PAL interlocal agreement (Item 7), New Cingular Wireless lease (Item 8), Durham Transit Center CMAR contract (Item 9), and bridge contracts (Items 14 and 17). Later in the session, Planning Director Sara Young discussed development review timelines, record rezoning caseloads, and equity/plain-language goals for the upcoming Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) rewrite before Council adjourned into closed session at 4:38 PM.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absence Approval, and Closed Session Motion (Womble Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal opened the work session with all seven members present and turned agenda management over to Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton. Council unanimously approved Javiera Caballero's excused absence request for January 3 and 5, 2023, and unanimously voted to enter closed session after regular business under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation on Willie Womble v. City of Durham and George Miller Jr. (Estate of Lorenzo Leathers Sr.).

agenda_items.title: Reading of Departmental Items, Pulled Items, and Transit Center Grant Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager Bo Ferguson flagged presentations for Item 3 (FY22 ACFR) and Item 12 (2022 Q3 Crime Report), and Middleton read Items 1–24. Council pulled Items 6 (Jillian Johnson), 7 (Middleton and DeDreana Freeman), 8, 9, 14, and 17 (Freeman), while Middleton praised the >$10 million FTA grant announced by Congressman Price for Durham Transit Center design with Perkins & Will (Item 10) and requested a timeline on the WIOA grant (Item 11). Subsequent presentations and pulled-item discussions were omitted in a truncated middle section of the digest.

agenda_items.title: Planning Review Turnaround Times and UDO Rewrite Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young responded to Council inquiries about development review durations, explaining staff review windows (5 days for simple items, 3 weeks initial for rezonings/site plans, 2 weeks for re-reviews) versus 90–180 day applicant resubmission cycles amid record caseloads. She outlined plans for the UDO rewrite to adopt plain language, deepen equity-focused community engagement, encourage local/smaller firm participation in RFP teams, and potentially add Tuesday public hearings to clear the case backlog.

agenda_items.title: Open Space & Trails Nomination, Mayor's Closing Remarks, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk nominated Melissa Souther for an At-Large seat on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission. Mayor Elaine O'Neal closed public business with remarks linking housing insecurity and lack of opportunity among young Black men to gun violence, urging community-wide investment beyond law enforcement before adjourning to closed session at 4:38 PM.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting Nov. 21 , 2022 (Livestream)
meetings.executive_summary: The November 21, 2022 regular City Council meeting opened with a proclamation for the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims—noting 149 traffic deaths in Durham from 2018 through October 2022 and featuring testimony from a resident whose husband was killed while biking on Guess Road—alongside a digital innovation award accepted by Mayor Pro Tempore Mark-Anthony Middleton. Council members rotated presiding duties across items after Mayor Elaine O'Neal and Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton noted upcoming December 5 and 8 excused travel. Although the middle portion of the transcript digest covering the consent agenda and earlier public hearings was truncated, the visible record shows Council passing six unanimous 7-0 votes across Item 34 (1402 Holloway Street zoning map change), Item 35 (Rhododendron Sewer and Lots consolidated annexation), and Item 36 (North Carolina Central University 24/7 Collaborative Learning and Resource Center rezoning).

agenda_items.title: Road Traffic Victims Remembrance Proclamation, Digital Award, and Travel Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All seven members answered roll call, and Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman read a proclamation for the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims citing 149 deaths since 2018 and Durham's Vision Zero commitment, followed by remarks from traffic-victim widow Ms. Simpson. Mayor Pro Tempore Middleton accepted a citywide IT award, requested excused absences for December 5 and 8 to visit Israel with an African-American leaders delegation, Mayor O'Neal noted December 5 travel to Selma, and Jillian Johnson circulated a draft ICAN nuclear weapons treaty resolution.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Updates and Recap of Nov. 10 Work Session Actions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted supplemental information on Items 15 (ArborMax) and 23 (NGE Services) and recapped Nov. 10 actions on Item 8 (Ward Redistricting presentation completed), Item 13 (HUD $40M Choice Neighborhoods grant approved 7-0 on Nov. 10), and Item 16 (505 W. Chapel Hill St.). The consent agenda and initial public hearings occurred within a truncated middle section of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 1402 Holloway Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: As the digest resumes under Javiera Caballero's presiding turn on the item preceding Items 35 and 36 (identified in the Nov. 10 work session agenda as Item 34, 1402 Holloway Street), Council voted 7-0 on the first motion and 7-0 to adopt the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Rhododendron Sewer and Lots
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presided over by Jillian Johnson, Planner Andy Lester presented a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and RS-20 initial zoning request for Kevin and Brandy Punt (prohibiting commercial and industrial development). Following brief public comment, Council approved both the annexation/UEA ordinance and the RS-20 Falls/Jordan District B zoning ordinance by 7-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: NCCU 24/7 Collaborative Learning and Resource Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Andy Lester and the applicant team (represented by Surface 678 PA / North Carolina Central University) presented a rezoning of three parcels at Lawson and Fayetteville Streets from RU-5 and UC-2 to UC-2(D) with a recommended future land use map change to Institutional. Dr. Monique Holsey-Hyman praised campus accessibility improvements and DeDreana Freeman expressed support before Council passed both the rezoning ordinance and the NCGS 160D-605 consistency statement 7-0, adjourning at 8:44 PM.

votes.notes: The reading of Motion 1 occurred immediately before the digest truncation cutoff at 01:20:30.
votes.discussion_detail: Passed Motion 1 on the agenda item immediately preceding Item 35 (Item 34, 1402 Holloway Street zoning map change per the Nov. 10 work session docket) by a 7-0 roll call vote.

votes.item_title: Item 34 (1402 Holloway Street Zoning Map Change) — Consistency Statement (NCGS 160D-605)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the consistency statement required by NCGS 160D-605 for Item 34.

votes.item_title: Item 35: Consolidated Annexation (Rhododendron Sewer and Lots) — Annexation Ordinance & UEA
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted an ordinance annexing Rhododendron Sewer and Lots into the City of Durham effective December 31, 2022, and authorizing the City Manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with Kevin Punt and Brandy Punt.

votes.item_title: Item 35: Consolidated Annexation (Rhododendron Sewer and Lots) — UDO Amendment to RS-20 F/J-B

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted an ordinance amending the UDO to rezone three parcels at Lawson and Fayetteville Streets from RU-5 and UC-2 to University and College 2 with a development plan (UC-2(D)).

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the consistency statement required by NCGS 160D-605 for the NCCU 24/7 Collaborative Learning and Resource Center rezoning.
