meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 21, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Elaine O'Neal presided over the December 21, 2021 Durham City Council work session with all seven members participating. Council unanimously approved priority items from the City Manager (7-0, referring Item 18 Griffin Place consolidated annexation back to administration and adding a code enforcement briefing), the City Attorney (7-0, scheduling a closed session for litigation updates in Tony Scott Jr. et al. v. City of Durham and Daryl Howard v. City of Durham), and the City Clerk (7-0, requesting virtual-meeting guidance for appointed boards). Following a Neighborhood Improvement Services briefing on code enforcement and landlord/tenant enforcement constraints, Council reviewed pulled consent items covering Legal Aid eviction defense, Southside Revitalization Phase 3, the DEAR expungement program, the Jordan Lake Western Intake Partnership, and C.M. Herndon Park soccer field change orders. During an extended work session review of Item 16 on the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) $51.8 million allocation, members debated how to balance staff-scored Tranche 1 proposals against reserving a second tranche for broader community-driven equity outreach, before reaching consensus that appointed boards should remain virtual during the Omicron surge and unanimously settling the January 3 agenda (7-0).

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page referred Item 18 (Griffin Place consolidated annexation) back to the administration and Planning Department and added a Neighborhood Improvement Services (NIS) code enforcement update. The City Attorney requested a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation on Tony Scott Jr. et al. v. City of Durham (20-CV-558) and Daryl Howard v. City of Durham (17-CV-477), and the City Clerk requested guidance on board and commission meeting formats amid the Omicron surge. Council approved all three priority item sets unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Improvement Services (NIS) Code Enforcement Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: NIS staff briefed Council on code enforcement inspection procedures, virtual hearing consent requirements, and statutory constraints on landlord enforcement and 30-day repair orders. Council members questioned how enforcement interacts with substandard rental properties and tenant complaints while avoiding incentives for landlords to defer repairs or displace tenants.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 3: Three-Year Grant Contract Amendment (#18353) with Legal Aid of North Carolina for Eviction Defense
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Member Charlie Reece, Item 3 reviewed expanded funding for Legal Aid of North Carolina's eviction diversion representation, including bilingual staffing, alongside community comments from Durham CAN and Legal Aid attorney Sarah D'Amato. Council Members Javiera Caballero, Jillian Johnson, DeDreana Freeman, and Reece discussed services for undocumented tenants (referred to Duke/NCCU clinics), landlord accountability at properties like Bradwell, and timing ahead of the January 3 vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (held for Jan. 3 agenda)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 5: Option Contract with Southside Revitalization Phase Three, LP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the third phase option contract for the Lofts at Southside development and discussed Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (9% LIHTC) application timelines, rezoning feasibility before the May deadline, and how it aligns with Willard Street Apartments Phase II.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (held for Jan. 3 agenda)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 6: Contract with Legal Aid of North Carolina for the Durham Expunction and Restoration (DEAR) Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Legal Aid attorney Gina Reyman and Community Safety Director Ryan Smith reported that DEAR had expunged over 1,000 charges since July across 18 counties, was building a petition generator, and was partnering on driver's license restoration and Raise the Age dismissals. Council Members Freeman, Leonardo Williams, Jillian Johnson, and Mayor Elaine O'Neal discussed job placement partnerships, Welcome Home reentry alignment, and collateral consequences of license revocations.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (held for Jan. 3 agenda)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 7: Capital Improvement Plan Ordinance Amendment for Jordan Lake Western Intake Partnership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Department of Water Management staff Jerry Morrone and Assistant Director Vicki Westbrook explained Durham's role as fiscal and contracting lead for the Western Intake Partnership due to holding the largest water allocation. Staff noted the regional project builds supply redundancy alongside the Williams Water Treatment Plant to meet 2050 demand projections with partners Pittsboro and Chatham County.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (held for Jan. 3 agenda)

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 12: Change Order #4 with GeoSurfaces Southeast Inc. for C.M. Herndon Park Soccer Field Conversion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton, General Services staff Rod Florence explained that the $50,000 change order addressed sub-base compaction failures uncovered after cutting soil to level the synthetic turf field. Council Member Freeman also confirmed the turf was plastic-based rather than recycled rubber tires.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (held for Jan. 3 agenda)

agenda_items.title: Presentation and Policy Discussion: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) of 2021 Allocation Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager Bertha Johnson reviewed Durham's $51.8 million ARPA allocation (which must be obligated by December 31, 2024 and spent by December 31, 2026) and staff scoring of community proposals. Mayor Elaine O'Neal and Council Members Charlie Reece, Javiera Caballero, Jillian Johnson, DeDreana Freeman, and Leonardo Williams debated funding high-scoring Tranche 1 proposals now versus reserving a second tranche for broader community co-design, demographic/geographic analysis, and Racial Equity Task Force-style facilitation.

agenda_items.title: Appointed Boards, Committees, and Commissions Virtual Meeting Guidance and Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Clerk Diana Schreiber sought guidance on in-person versus virtual meetings for Council-appointed boards amid rising COVID-19 Omicron cases. Council expressed informal thumbs-up consensus that all boards and commissions should remain virtual alongside Council, then voted unanimously to settle the January 3, 2022 agenda (consent items 1–15 and public hearings 17 and 19) before entering closed session.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items (Referral of Item 18 Griffin Place Annexation and Addition of NIS Code Enforcement Update)
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call with all seven council members present.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager Wanda Page recommended referring Item 18 back to the administration and Planning Department and adding an NIS briefing on code enforcement.

votes.item_title: City Attorney's Priority Item: Closed Session for Attorney-Client Consultation (Scott v. City of Durham and Howard v. City of Durham)
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to hold a closed session at the end of the work session regarding Tony Scott Jr. et al. v. City of Durham (20-CV-558) and Daryl Howard v. City of Durham (17-CV-477).

votes.item_title: Approval of City Clerk's Priority Item (Board/Commission Omicron Meeting Format Discussion)
votes.notes: Unanimous roll call vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Added the City Clerk's request to discuss virtual versus in-person meeting guidance for appointed boards, committees, and commissions.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 21, 2021
disagreements.issue: ARPA Funding Allocation Pace: Tranche 1 Scoring vs. Second-Round Community Co-Design
disagreements.summary: During the ARPA work session presentation, Council members differed over how much of Durham's remaining ARPA funds to award immediately based on staff rubric scores versus holding back in a second tranche for broader community engagement and targeted equity goals.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance a substantial first tranche of top-scoring projects (such as those scoring 24–25+ points) to avoid delaying urgent community relief while reserving a clear dollar target for a second round.
side_a_arguments: Charlie Reece argued staff built a strong rubric and suggested narrowing Tranche 1 to the highest-scoring proposals to establish a concrete dollar figure for Tranche 2.
Staff noted ARPA funds must be obligated by December 31, 2024 and spent by December 31, 2026.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pause or limit immediate awards until Council receives demographic and geographic breakdowns and designs a broader, expert-facilitated community process for lasting impact.
side_b_arguments: Mayor Elaine O'Neal, Javiera Caballero, Jillian Johnson, DeDreana Freeman, and Leonardo Williams emphasized equitable demographic/geographic targeting, sustainable systems rather than one-off allocations, and bringing in community engagement facilitation similar to the Racial Equity Task Force.
Members requested a categorized breakdown of existing proposals by demographics, geography, and issue area before finalizing tranche sizes.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; staff was directed to compile demographic, geographic, and category breakdowns of proposals for further Council deliberation.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec. 20. 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Meeting virtually on December 20, 2021 amid rising COVID-19 Omicron cases, all seven Durham City Council members discussed displacement and utility shutoffs affecting tenants of Braswell Properties alongside upcoming January 2022 reporting on Bull City Tenants United proposals and rental housing code enforcement. Council unanimously passed the Consent Agenda 7-0, approving the FY2021 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, a Bob Barker Company Foundation grant for Durham's guaranteed income pilot, police fleet and Axon camera contracts, watershed conservation funding, and public works contracts. Following a continued public hearing, Council unanimously approved a 7-0 rezoning and FLUM amendment (plus consistency statement) for 518 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway from CG(D) to RSMD for up to 173 apartments, conditioned on new proffers of $50,000 to the Affordable Housing Fund and $500 per projected additional Durham Public Schools student.

agenda_items.title: Omicron Surge Precautions, Braswell Properties Tenant Crisis, and Housing Advocacy Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council opened with roll call confirming all seven members present virtually due to the Omicron variant surge and discussed severe habitability and pending displacement crises affecting approximately 12 families renting from Braswell Properties without heat or electricity. Members noted a community press conference attended by Charlie Reece, Leonardo Williams, and Javiera Caballero, shared Trinity Avenue Presbyterian Church's tenant relief fund, and highlighted upcoming January 2022 staff reports responding to Bull City Tenants United.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page reported that Neighborhood Improvement Services would brief Council at the December 21 work session on rental housing code compliance, and highlighted updates to Item 9 (FY2021 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report) and Item 13 (EMA Resources Inc. five-year biosolids contract CPI adjustment provision). The City Attorney and City Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Approval of FY2021 ACFR, Guaranteed Income Pilot Grant, Police Fleet/Body Cameras, Watersheds, and Infrastructure Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered the Consent Agenda encompassing the FY2021 ACFR audit, a Bob Barker Company Foundation grant for the guaranteed income pilot, Holloway Street/NC 98 safety improvements, water tank maintenance with Classic Protective Coatings, EMA Resources biosolids disposal, Hydromax USA valve auditing, Tar River and Triangle Land Conservancy watershed grants, Finance Officer and Tax Collector appointments, 29 police sedans, Axon body-worn and in-car camera contracts, Morris & McDaniel promotional testing, and the Northeast Creek septic-to-sewer cost share. No items were pulled, and Council approved the slate unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 518 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway (CG(D) to RSMD, Up to 173 Apartments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming a public hearing continued from December 6, planning staff and applicants Dan Jewell (Coulter Jewell Thames), Mark Galifianakis, and James Bradford presented a 9.651-acre rezoning from Commercial General with a Development Plan to Residential Suburban Multifamily with a Development Plan for up to 173 apartments on land sold by New Creation United Methodist Church. During the hearing, the applicant added proffers of $50,000 to the Affordable Housing Fund and $500 per additional projected DPS student (estimated at 37 students). Council members debated losing commercial land on MLK Parkway and discussed workforce-housing affordability thresholds before approving the rezoning and statutory consistency statement unanimously.

votes.item_title: Item 27 — Adopt Zoning Map Change Ordinance and FLUM Amendment for 518 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway (CG(D) to RSMD)
votes.discussion_detail: Following applicant proffers of $50,000 to the Affordable Housing Fund and $500 per projected DPS student, Mark-Anthony Middleton moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded adopting the ordinance rezoning 9.651 acres at 518 MLK Jr. Parkway to RSMD for up to 173 apartments and amending the Future Land Use Map. All seven council members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Item 27 — Adopt NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for 518 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway
votes.discussion_detail: Javiera Caballero moved and DeDreana Freeman seconded adopting the statutory NCGS 160D-605 statement of consistency for the 518 MLK Jr. Parkway rezoning. Council approved the motion 7-0 by roll call.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Dec. 20. 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Loss of Commercial Land vs. Workforce Multifamily Housing at 518 MLK Jr. Parkway
disagreements.summary: During the 518 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway hearing, council members weighed concerns about shrinking commercial zoning along a major transit corridor and securing binding affordability commitments against adding 173 workforce-oriented apartments near the American Tobacco Trail.
disagreements.side_a_position: Push for deeper community benefits and evaluate whether rezoning commercial land reduces future neighborhood-serving commercial capacity.
side_a_arguments: Converting commercially designated corridor parcels to multifamily housing permanently reduces future neighborhood retail/service sites.
Council members pressed for concrete school and affordable housing fund proffers and clarity on AMI rent affordability.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support the RSMD rezoning as market-rate workforce housing paired with American Tobacco Trail connectivity and newly added cash proffers.
side_b_arguments: Site was formerly a church use and developer added $50,000 for affordable housing plus $500 per projected DPS student.
Durham urgently needs rental housing supply near employment centers and trail infrastructure.
disagreements.resolution: After the applicant added the $50,000 affordable housing proffer and $500-per-student DPS commitment during the hearing, Council voted unanimously 7-0 to approve the rezoning.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 9, 2021 at 1 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: This original live-stream recording captures the December 9, 2021 Work Session—Mayor Elaine O'Neal and Council Member Leonardo Williams' first work session—beginning mid-announcements at Charlie Reece's nature-preserve request and covering identical substantive business to the corrected-audio upload. Council unanimously approved 7-0 all three priority-item motions (including joining LA's Fifth Circuit DACA amicus brief and deferring Items 1-8 appointments to January 6), reviewed pulled Consent items, heard citizen speakers on 911 wait times and firefighter pay, and received Cherry Bekaert's FY2021 ACFR audit and Chief Patrice Andrews' Q3 2021 crime report. Council then voted 7-0 to reschedule the December 23 work session to December 21 and set the December 20 regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: DOST/EAB Nature Preserve Proposal, NC Tuition Assistance, and New Council Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stream opens during Charlie Reece's announcement requesting January 6 agenda placement for a DOST/EAB/ECWA nature preserve presentation, followed by Leonardo Williams sharing NC community college tuition assistance ($2,800 over two years via yourhighereducation.com), Mayor Pro Tem Mark-Anthony Middleton's inaugural remarks, and Mayor Elaine O'Neal thanking staff for onboarding.

agenda_items.title: City Manager, City Attorney (DACA Amicus Brief), and City Clerk (Defer Items 1-8) Priority Actions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 on three priority-item motions: referring Items 15-16 (Western Intake contracts) back to the administration and adding Items 26-27; authorizing Durham to join Los Angeles and LA County's Fifth Circuit DACA amicus brief in Texas v. United States; and deferring board/commission appointment Items 1-8 to January 6, 2022.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Items 11, 12, 23 and Citizen Concerns on 911 Vacancies & Firefighter Pay
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members reviewed the consent docket—praising Item 10 (Bob Barker Foundation guaranteed income grant) and Items 17-18 watershed grants—and heard Citizen Matters speakers Brandon Rich (911 call-taker vacancy and pay) and Rebecca Ponce de Leon (182 firefighters below living wage across a 56-hour week), before reviewing pulled Items 11, 12, and 23.

agenda_items.title: FY2021 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) Audit & HR Director Farewell
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following farewell remarks for retiring HR Director Regina Youngblood, Cherry Bekaert auditors Jermaine Brewington and April Adams presented the FY2021 ACFR, reporting unmodified audit opinions, one significant year-end cutoff deficiency, and a 29.8% unassigned General Fund balance after adding $19.6M.

agenda_items.title: 2021 Q3 Crime Report and Temporary Patrol Reassignments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Patrice Andrews reported an 11% reduction in Part I violent crime alongside a 58% increase in homicides (38 in nine months) and 87% sworn staffing, outlining temporary January-March patrol reassignments and answering council questions on mental health peer support, U-visas, and upcoming January police pay adjustments.

agenda_items.title: Move Dec. 23 Work Session to Dec. 21, COVID-19 Meeting Metrics, and Set Dec. 20 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to move the December 23 work session to December 21, tasked Jillian Johnson and Mayor O'Neal with consulting Public Health Director Rod Jenkins and county officials on objective COVID-19 virtual-meeting thresholds, noted the January 6 deferral of Bull City Tenants United reporting, and approved the December 20 agenda 7-0.

votes.item_title: Accept City Manager Priority Items (Refer Back Items 15-16; Add Items 26-27)
votes.notes: Original live-stream recording corresponding to zUxp0rExee8.
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Jillian Johnson seconded the City Manager's priority requests referring Items 15-16 back and adding Items 26-27. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Accept City Attorney Priority Item — Join Fifth Circuit Amicus Brief Supporting DACA (Texas v. United States)
votes.discussion_detail: Following City Attorney Kim Rehberg's presentation on joining Los Angeles's Fifth Circuit amicus brief defending DACA, DeDreana Freeman moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded approval. Passed 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Accept City Clerk Priority Item — Defer Board/Commission Appointment Items 1-8 to January 6, 2022
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Leonardo Williams seconded deferring board and commission appointment Items 1-8 to the January 6, 2022 work session. Passed 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Move December 23 Work Session to Tuesday, December 21, 2021
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded rescheduling the December 23 work session to Tuesday, December 21, 2021. Passed 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for December 20, 2021 Regular Meeting (Consent: 9-14, 17-23; Public Hearing: 27)
votes.discussion_detail: DeDreana Freeman moved and Javiera Caballero seconded approving the December 20 regular meeting docket (Consent 9-14 and 17-23; GBA Public Hearing Item 27). Passed 7-0 by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session Dec. 9, 2021 at 1 p.m. (Live Stream)
disagreements.issue: Contractor Attendance for Equity/MWBE Questioning & COVID-19 Virtual Meeting Thresholds
disagreements.summary: Council members exchanged views on requiring contractor visibility during work sessions on pulled MWBE items (Item 12) and how to coordinate objective COVID-19 thresholds across City Hall and Durham County before reverting to virtual sessions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Seek prompt data-driven COVID-19 positivity guidelines from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins and improve contractor accountability.
side_a_arguments: Positivity near 5% before holidays requires pre-set thresholds so future shifts to virtual meetings are non-arbitrary.
Contractors should appear virtually to answer questions about equity and MWBE participation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Involve County officials alongside staff briefings while new members complete orientation.
side_b_arguments: Mayor O'Neal and Council Member Williams emphasized learning briefings before setting policies and looping in County leadership.
disagreements.resolution: Jillian Johnson agreed to coordinate an informational email inquiry with Public Health Director Rod Jenkins, City Manager Page, and County leadership.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Dec. 6, 2021 at 7 p.m. (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: The live-stream video of the December 6, 2021 Organizational and Regular Meeting begins mid-ceremony during Council Member Leonardo Williams' swearing-in and captures Mayor Elaine O'Neal's oath of office and inaugural address before Council unanimously elected Mark-Anthony Middleton as Mayor Pro Tempore. Following a brief recess, Council voted 7-0 to approve Consent Items 1-3, 6-9, and 11-16 (excluding Item 10). At Mayor O'Neal's request to allow newly seated members time for staff briefings and UNC School of Government training, Council concurred without objection to continue public hearings for Item 18 (2211 Page Road) to January 3 and Item 19 (518 MLK Jr. Parkway) to December 20, and then approved Item 10 (Durham Athletic Park 9th Amendment) 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Swearing-In Ceremonies for Leonardo Williams and Mayor Elaine O'Neal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The live stream starts during Judge Carl Fox's administration of Leonardo Williams' oath of office, followed by Williams' remarks, Mayor Elaine O'Neal's swearing-in ceremony, and O'Neal's inaugural address pledging inclusive leadership across all neighborhoods.

agenda_items.title: Nomination and Election of Mark-Anthony Middleton as Mayor Pro Tempore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor O'Neal nominated Mark-Anthony Middleton for Mayor Pro Tempore, which passed unanimously by voice vote. Following his oath of office, Council recessed until 8:00 PM.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Audits, Bikeway Study, Housing Grants, Built2Last MOU, and Debris Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon reconvening, DeDreana Freeman acknowledged World AIDS Day, City Manager Wanda Page noted a page-number revision on Item 18, and Council unanimously approved Consent Items 1-3, 6-9, and 11-16 (with Item 10 held aside for speaker cards).

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation — 2211 Page Road (67 Townhomes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Alexander Cahill's staff report on the 10.15-acre OI(D) townhome annexation at 2211 Page Road, Mayor O'Neal asked colleagues to continue the hearing to January 3, 2022 so she and Council Member Williams could receive departmental briefings and attend UNC Institute of Government training; Council concurred without objection.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change — 518 Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway (173 Apartments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Danny Cultra's staff report on 518 MLK Jr. Parkway (CG(D) to RSMD), Mayor O'Neal requested continuing the public hearing until December 20, 2021 to give newly seated members additional preparation time; Council concurred without objection.

agenda_items.title: Ninth Amendment Assignment Agreement for Durham Athletic Park Operating Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After the City Clerk explained that speaker cards listed under Item 10 contained a typo meant for Item 19, Council voted unanimously 7-0 to approve the Durham Athletic Park Operating Agreement Ninth Amendment.

votes.item_title: Elect Mark-Anthony Middleton as Mayor Pro Tempore
votes.notes: Live-stream recording corresponding to audio upload VJXHLBmJ1HU.
votes.discussion_detail: Mayor O'Neal nominated Mark-Anthony Middleton as Mayor Pro Tempore; following an unnamed motion and second, Council unanimously approved the election by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Item 10 — Ninth Amendment Assignment Agreement for Durham Athletic Park Operating Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Charlie Reece moved and Mark-Anthony Middleton seconded approval of Item 10 after the clerk clarified the speaker-card typo meant Item 19. Passed 7-0 via chamber electronic voting.
